items.title: Oregon sues OpenAI for at least $2.035 billion over ChatGPT child-safety failures
items.summary: Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield announced a suit against OpenAI in Multnomah County Circuit Court seeking at least $2.035 billion. Claims: unlawful trade practices (misleading consumers about ChatGPT's safety for children and teens), negligence, unjust enrichment and public nuisance. The complaint cites harmful interactions involving suicide, self-harm, eating disorders and violence. OpenAI points to its parental controls. Allegations only.
items.why_it_matters: State attorneys general now seek billions from a leading AI vendor, raising legal risk for consumer-facing AI.

items.title: US 'jobless growth': strong GDP and AI investment but weak hiring and a record-low labour share
items.summary: Fortune reports Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualised while employers added an average of 48,000 jobs a month over the 12 months to September, then 165,000 in October. Goldman Sachs estimates AI spending drove more than half of business-investment growth in the first three quarters of 2026. Labour's share of output fell to 53.0% in Q3, the lowest since 1947. Unemployment among 20-24 year-olds is 7.5%, against 4.1% overall.
items.why_it_matters: AI-driven investment lifts output while hiring and labour share lag; young workers bear the burden.

items.title: Australia: unemployment hits 4.9% as job cuts spread and AI is seen as a factor; APRA to stress-test AI scenarios
items.summary: ABC reports Australian unemployment rose to 4.9% in October, with employment down 43,500 and mass layoffs across retail, banking, airlines and tech. The article gives no data on AI's share of job losses. Financial regulator APRA will run stress tests on hypothetical AI-related scenarios for banks, super funds and insurers.
items.why_it_matters: Regulators start treating AI-related shocks as systemic risk; causal link to AI is speculative.
